channels.title: The Price of One Percent
channels.style: Animated financial explainer, navy, mint and cream, precise labeled arithmetic
channels.description: An illustrative comparison of annual investment fees on a constant $10,000 balance. 1% = $100, 0.25% = $25, difference = $75. Actual balances and charges vary. Educational content, not personalized investment advice.

scenes.heading: THE PRICE OF 1%
scenes.text: One percent sounds tiny. On a ten thousand dollar investment, it can mean one hundred dollars in annual fees.

scenes.heading: KEEP THE EXAMPLE SIMPLE
scenes.text: For this simple example, hold the account value constant. We are comparing costs, not predicting investment returns.

scenes.heading: SAME BALANCE. DIFFERENT FEE.
scenes.text: A quarter percent fee would cost twenty five dollars. That's seventy five dollars less for that year.

scenes.heading: SMALL COSTS ADD UP
scenes.text: Fees also leave less money invested to earn future returns. Over time, that difference can grow.

scenes.heading: CHECK THE WHOLE PICTURE
scenes.text: Before comparing investments, check ongoing fees, trading charges, and what service you receive. Lower cost alone does not mean lower risk.

scenes.heading: KNOW WHAT YOU PAY
scenes.text: Returns are uncertain. Costs deserve your attention.

channels.title: Lila and the Little Lantern
channels.style: Original gentle 2D storybook animation, one consistent red fox with a green leaf hat and one gray owl with a blue scarf
channels.description: Original fiction for children ages 4–7. A little fox returns Owl's lantern, and a kind friend lights the way home. Calm narration and a reassuring ending.

scenes.heading: A LITTLE LIGHT
scenes.text: Lila the fox found a little lantern beside the path. Its warm light flickered in the evening breeze.

scenes.heading: SOMEONE NEEDS IT
scenes.text: Someone must be missing this, she thought. She lifted it gently and followed the trail toward Owl's tree.

scenes.heading: A FRIEND UP ABOVE
scenes.text: Owen peered from his doorway. My lantern! I couldn't find my way down in the dark.

scenes.heading: A KIND LITTLE FOX
scenes.text: Lila set the lantern on his doorstep. Owen came down slowly, smiling at his little friend.

scenes.heading: LET ME HELP YOU
scenes.text: Thank you, he said. Shall I light your way home? Lila nodded, her tail swishing happily.

scenes.heading: GOODNIGHT, LILA
scenes.text: Together they followed the golden glow. Soon Lila was snug in her den, and the forest settled into sleep.

channels.title: The Wrong Key
channels.style: Original atmospheric 2D suspense animation, first-person locked door, phone and key, coherent supernatural payoff, no gore
channels.description: Original fictional horror. A call from inside a locked apartment reveals what the key in the narrator's hand really is. Suspense and a supernatural ending; no claim of real events.

scenes.heading: THE WRONG KEY
scenes.text: At midnight, I stood outside my locked apartment. My phone rang. The caller was me.

scenes.heading: STILL IN MY HAND
scenes.text: A voice whispered, you left your key on the kitchen table. But my key was in my hand.

scenes.heading: SOMETHING INSIDE
scenes.text: Then a key scraped against wood on the other side of the door. I stopped breathing.

scenes.heading: LOOK AT YOUR PALM
scenes.text: Look at your palm, the voice said. Slowly, the brass key in my hand began turning black.

scenes.heading: THAT ISN'T YOUR KEY
scenes.text: The thing inside laughed with my voice. That's not your key, it whispered. That's my tooth.

scenes.heading: IT WAS SMILING
scenes.text: Something sharp unfolded against my skin. Behind the door, a mouth full of keys began to smile.
